title: Event Hubs: partitions, consumer groups and capture into storage

videos.script: Quitanda's app reports every tap a customer makes. A page opened, a banana added to the cart, a checkout started. {{taps}} Those clicks arrive by the hundred every second, all day. The fraud check wants them within seconds. The analysts want every one of them in the lake by morning. {{readers}} On Azure, that is Event Hubs. An event hub is not one queue. It is a set of partitions, and each partition is an ordered log of its own. {{partitions}} You will send clicks to the emulator on your laptop and find out where each customer's clicks landed. {{send}} Then you will read them back twice, with two consumer groups that never get in each other's way. {{groups}} A reader remembers where it stopped with a checkpoint. You will find that checkpoint as a small blob in Azurite. {{checkpoint}} Last come the parts the emulator does not have. Capture copies the stream into storage on its own, and the tier decides what all of it costs. {{capture}}
